title: The Memory Master Challenge
clue: The prize is hidden in plain sight, but the wait between seeing it and running for it is the whole test.
reveal: Your dog watches you hide one prize in one of four spots, then you both take a slow lap of the room before the release. Does your dog remember where it went? Spoiler: the tail will tell you.
objective: Hide one prize where your dog can see, take a short lap together, and release your dog to find it from memory.
instructions: Set four spots in one room or a hallway, three steps apart: a mat, an open cardboard box, a chair seat and a basket. Make sure the floor is non-slip. You need five tiny soft treats or a favorite small toy.
Show your dog the prize, then tuck it into one spot while they watch, at their pace. Say nothing about it.
The lap: walk once around the room together at a normal pace, a short loop, ending at the starting point. Start with just a few seconds between hide and release.
Say 'go find' and let your dog go. Whatever spot they choose, wait. If it is right, celebrate and let them have the prize. If it is wrong, stay cheerful: they may try again on their own.
Round two: change the spot, then make the lap a little longer, with a sniff stop on the way. Stop after three or four rounds so it stays a game.
Bonus round: hide two prizes in two different spots in view, then see which your dog remembers first. Ask for no order.
Finish with a free-for-all: sprinkle a handful of treats in the open room and let your dog sniff them up.
twist: Your dog sees the hiding and must hold the memory through a slow lap together before the release, so it is remembering, not sniffing.
variations: Easier: release at once, no lap.
Small apartment: use two spots only and a lap around the sofa.
Harder: a 20-second lap that includes a stop to say hello to the window.
Ball-obsessed dog: swap the prize for a favorite chew, never thrown.
completion: Counts when your dog has visited a spot after the lap. Getting it wrong is part of the game; no scores are kept.
photoIdea: Your dog standing in the middle of the room pointing a nose at the right spot.
memoryPrompt: Which spot did they check first, and did they ever second-guess themselves?
supplies: A mat, a box, a chair and a basket
Tiny soft treats or a small toy
dietNotes: Tiny treats from the daily ration; check labels for xylitol. Ask your vet about diet limits.
safety: Non-slip floor only; use rugs or a mat on tile or wood and skip any slippery room.
Keep each round short and end on a find. Supervise any box or basket.
